title: Washington-Youree Hotel in Shreveport during the depression
summary: Through Gordon Tulley he joined Flem Ferguson's hotel band in Shreveport, paid only room, food allowance and occasional gigs, yet remembered it as a happy time.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: that's when I decided to investigate the south. I'd heard so much about all these guys coming out of there, you know, Teagarden and Louis Armstrong out of New Orleans, and so I went -- I got -- I had a friend of mine, a trumpet player who had played in that band that was on the S. S. Pennland, a fellow by the name of Gordon Tulley, and he was working with Flem Ferguson and the Washington-Erie Hotel in Shreveport, Louisiana, and he got me on the band there, and well, that was a delightful job. We -- for our work at the hotel we got our room, $10.50 a week allowance for food in the coffee shop, and no money. The only way we got any cash at all was, see, we only played a noon session and a dinner session, and the only way we got any money at all was on Saturday night we'd play at the country club and we'd get seven bucks or something like that, or if you could pick up some other place to play, individually, you know, not as a band, you might pick up another night in some little joint there for four or five bucks, and that was the only way we got any money.
Was that a fairly big hotel?
Oh, yes. It's -- it was the biggest hotel in town. In fact it was a combination of two hotels. They were connected.
Was that a common practice for big hotels to pay so little, I mean to pay nothing?
Well, you have to remember this was at

the height of the depression, and to have a band at all was a complete luxury, and I can't speak for -- I've heard of some funny stories about some of the deals these bands had. This to me is the worst deal I've heard of. However, you want to know something? I can't remember a happier time in my life than those days at the Washington-Erie.
Why, were you playing great music, or just having a good time, or --
